Lesson objective
Solve quadratic equations by rewriting them as a product equal to zero. Every root must satisfy the original equation.
Zero-product property
If A times B equals zero, then at least one factor is zero. This is why factoring can turn a quadratic into two simpler equations.
Put everything on one side
Before factoring, move all terms so the equation equals zero. For example x squared plus two x equals fifteen becomes x squared plus two x minus fifteen equals zero.
Find integer factors
To factor x squared minus five x plus six, choose numbers that multiply to six and add to negative five. Negative two and negative three work.
Solve both factors
Write x minus two times x minus three equals zero. Solve x minus two equals zero and x minus three equals zero to get two and three.
Check by substitution
At x equals two, four minus ten plus six is zero. At x equals three, nine minus fifteen plus six is also zero.
Greatest common factor first
For three x squared minus twelve x equals zero, factor three x times x minus four. The roots are zero and four; never divide away the x factor.
Difference of squares
Four x squared minus thirty-six equals zero factors as four times x minus three times x plus three. The solutions are negative three and three.
Nonmonic trinomials
Two x squared plus seven x plus three factors as two x plus one times x plus three. The solutions are negative one half and negative three.
Word problem

If a rectangle has sides x plus two and x plus five and area fifty-four, form x squared plus seven x minus forty-four equals zero. Factor x plus eleven times x minus four, and keep the positive root four.
Advanced challenge
Treat x to the fourth minus thirteen x squared plus thirty-six as a quadratic in u equals x squared. Solve u equals four or nine, then take both positive and negative square roots.
Exam recap
Set the equation equal to zero, factor completely, solve every factor, check the original equation, and apply any restrictions from the question.
